title: One photon, several carefully labeled scales
question: How can one stated photon frequency determine energy and vacuum wavelength, then support equivalent mass and temperature labels without changing what the photon is?
answerPreview: Use E_gamma = h nu and lambda_vac = c/nu for the photon and its vacuum propagation, then label E_gamma/c^2 and E_gamma/k_B only as equivalent scales, not photon rest mass or a thermal state.
summary: Keep photon vacuum identities separate from energy-equivalent mass and temperature coordinates, preserve the stated input-frequency uncertainty boundary, and avoid physical-state claims that the equations do not support.

observationStage.title: Exact International System of Units (SI) constants used by the bridge
observationStage.question: Which constants are exact, and what information must still come from the source?

items.label: Planck constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes h exactly; multiplying it by a stated cyclic frequency gives one photon's energy through E_gamma = h nu.

items.label: Speed of light in vacuum
items.explanation: The SI fixes c exactly; lambda_vac = c/nu applies to propagation in vacuum.

items.label: Boltzmann constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes k_B exactly; dividing energy by k_B labels an equivalent temperature scale without specifying a thermal ensemble.

observationStage.conclusion: The bridge constants have exact SI values, but the frequency is a stated input or illustrative preset. Without an input-frequency uncertainty, the activity reports no propagated uncertainty and does not turn a source choice into an exact spectral observation.

guidedBlocks.title: Start with the photon and vacuum equations
body: A photon with stated cyclic frequency nu has energy E_gamma = h nu.
For propagation in vacuum, its wavelength is lambda_vac = c/nu. A wavelength in matter would require the material response and is not this vacuum identity.
The radio, microwave, visible-blue, X-ray, and gamma-ray choices are illustrative presets. Spectral-band boundaries are conventions, not SI definitions.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Fixed h and c; photon energy and vacuum propagation relationships
caveats: The activity uses cyclic frequency, not angular frequency.

guidedBlocks.title: Equivalent is a label, not a new physical state
body: Dividing the photon energy by c squared gives an energy-equivalent mass scale m_equiv = E_gamma/c^2.
That label does not assign a nonzero rest mass to the photon. A photon in vacuum is not being placed at rest by this conversion.
Dividing by k_B gives T_equiv = E_gamma/k_B. This compares energy coordinates; it does not claim that the photon is a thermal system or that a material has that temperature.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md, 2026-07-26 contract
caveats: Mass-equivalent and temperature-equivalent values are not independent observations.

technicalBlocks.title: The bridge is one algebraic map
body: For a positive stated nu, direct substitution gives E_gamma = h nu and lambda_vac = c/nu.
Substituting E_gamma gives m_equiv = h nu/c^2 and T_equiv = h nu/k_B. All four outputs therefore share one input and are correlated identities, not four independent measurements.
The implementation evaluates each expression once with finite floating-point arithmetic and does not fit parameters or load a dataset.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; tour-photon-bridge-v1 contract
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Photon bridge equation and immediate-evaluation contract
caveats: Finite floating-point values are not mathematically exact digit strings even when the SI constants are exact.

technicalBlocks.title: The source frequency controls the uncertainty boundary
body: If nu has relative standard uncertainty u(nu)/nu, then these one-input identities inherit that relative uncertainty in E_gamma, m_equiv, and T_equiv; lambda_vac has the same relative magnitude under first-order propagation.
The activity accepts no uncertainty field, so it must not invent output uncertainties or describe the values as measured results.
The vacuum wavelength equation excludes dispersion and refractive index. Equivalent temperature excludes occupation statistics, emissivity, and thermodynamic equilibrium.
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Uncertainty reporting convention and photon bridge domain boundary
caveats: First-order relative-uncertainty statements assume the one-variable identity model and a sufficiently small input uncertainty.
